Macrons

Consonantal i

Consonantal u

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

yourself pronoun

also by yourself, you yourself, look after yourself

classical

Cic. Att. 1.5.8: tibi persuādeās

tē, tibi (reflexive)

pronoun: the ordinary forms of tū, used reflexively

yourself (as object)

As with “myself”, there is no separate reflexive: tē servā, save yourself; tēcum, with yourself. Often no pronoun at all: “look after yourself” is cūrā ut valeās.

Other words

  • ipse, ipsa, ipsum — yourself (for emphasis: you yourself)

    pronoun, intensive · classical · Hor. Ep. 1.2.33: ut tē ipsum servēs; Cic. Fam. 9.14.8: fac ut dīligentissimē tē ipsum custōdiās (Lewis & Short, s.v. ipse) · Declension on Wiktionary

    Agrees with tū when it stresses the doer (tūte ipse, you did it yourself), with tē when it stresses the object: ut tē ipsum servēs, to save yourself (and not something else).

  • tūte — you yourself, you and no one else

    pronoun: tū with the suffix -te · also used · classical · Ter. Ph. 318: Tūte hoc intrīstī; Enn. in Gell. 2.29.20: quod tūte agere possiēs

Examples

  • ut tē ipsum servēs, nōn expergīsceris?

    Won’t you wake up to save yourself?Hor. Ep. 1.2.33

  • Tūte hoc intrīstī: tibi omne est exedendum.

    You cooked this up yourself: you must eat it all up.Ter. Ph. 318

  • cūrā ut valeās et nōs amēs et tibi persuādeās tē ā mē frāternē amārī

    Look after yourself, love us, and be sure that I love you like a brother.Cic. Att. 1.5.8

  • hoc erit tibi argūmentum semper in prōmptū situm: nē quid expectēs amīcōs, quod tūte agere possiēs

    Keep this lesson always at hand: don’t expect your friends to do what you can do yourself.Enn. in Gell. 2.29.20

  • fac ut dīligentissimē tē ipsum custōdiās

    Take the greatest care of yourself.Cic. Fam. 9.14.8 (Lewis & Short)

See also you, myself, yourselves, oneself.
